actor.name: NAME
actor.cycleTrait: Set the state by hand: intact, dented, broken. To undo a misclick.
actor.risqueHint: Big Shot's pool, earned at setup and spent to harden tests.
actor.resetSessionHint: Sets the movement back to the first, and empties the whole table's cartons and false notes.
actor.resetSessionConfirm: Set the movement back to OK, and empty this prime's false notes along with its {hunters} hunters' cartons? None of this can be recovered.
actor.activePrimeHint: This prime receives the false notes produced by rolls.
actor.inactivePrimeHint: Activating this prime automatically replaces the current one.
actor.notesHint: Roll false notes are credited here while this prime is active. The GM can correct each pool with + and −.
actor.noActivePrime: No prime is in play. The GM has to choose one.
actor.playerCartonsHint: The prime may hold a GM-managed reserve for tests or bonuses. Each hunter holding cartons gets a row, followed by totals grouped by genre.

session.title: Session
session.hint: The GM writes these lines before play and turns them over as they come into play. Until a line is revealed, players do not see it on this sheet.

riffs.title: Riffs
riffs.hint: The gameplay actions the session type opens, for the mouvement being played. Big Shot decides which ones are on the table.
riffs.editorHint: Tick, mouvement by mouvement, what the session opens. The book has riffs accumulate — what opens at one mouvement stays open at the next — but nothing here forces you to.
riffs.none: No riff is on the table for this mouvement.
riffs.customDescriptionPlaceholder: What it allows, and what it costs…

effects.minimumNotes: false notes at the very least
effects.disadvantageDoubleCarton: a double other than 6 grants a carton

riffs.correctionHint: Not a riff but a base rule, and the first thing a filler session moves over to rhythm. The player picks one of the listed payments.
riffs.bespokeEffects: This riff is hard-wired: its price is editable, its effects are not.
riffs.owedHint: Paid by another hunter, who takes it off their own sheet. The system records it and reminds you.
riffs.notCounted: Taken from the test, not from a sheet: cannot be checked in advance.
riffs.noEffect: This riff would change nothing about this result.
riffs.totalCostNone: No riff played: this test costs nothing.
riffs.openNone: No riff open at this mouvement.
riffs.assistOwed: {name} owes {cost}, to be taken off their own sheet.
riffs.healHint: Up to {count} damage on your own traits. Severe damage cannot be cleared this way, and a MONO's traits are repaired on its own sheet.
riffs.approachHint: Its traits join the pool. The genre bonus stays with the test's own approach.
riffs.soloUsed: Solo! has already been played this session.
riffs.noCarton: This prime has no genre: the carton could not be credited.

involve.name: Get involved
involve.description: Tick a cartridge to add two dice to your pool.

showWounds.name: Show your wounds
showWounds.description: Roll with disadvantage, describing how your damage makes life harder: once resolved, clear up to two damages from the traits described. Severe damage cannot be cleared this way.

force.name: Force it
force.description: Right after the roll, if you did not get both cartons, trigger two false notes to make one.

doubleOrNothing.name: Double or nothing
doubleOrNothing.description: Ignore the first roll and throw again with one more die, putting a trait at stake. Without both cartons that trait is struck out until the end of the session; the second result stands, better or worse.

solo.name: Solo!
solo.description: Once per session, spend a rhythm point before or after a test: you gain and immediately spend a carton, even if you take no part in the test.

assist.name: Assist
assist.description: Spend a rhythm point to grant advantage to another hunter's test. Once it is resolved, clear the damage on one of your traits.

improvise.name: Improvise
improvise.description: Spend a rhythm point to use traits from a second approach in your test.

jam.name: Jam!
jam.description: Like assisting, but you also lend your groove to the test. You likewise clear the damage on one of your traits once it is resolved.

risqueNote.name: False note
risqueNote.description: Spend a risk to add one false note to a test's result, and use it immediately.

risqueDisadvantage.name: Disadvantage
risqueDisadvantage.description: Spend a risk to impose disadvantage on a test.

risqueDoubleNote.name: Double false note
risqueDoubleNote.description: Spend a risk to add two false notes to a test's result. They must be used immediately and earn no risk.

groove.title: Groove
groove.audienceHint: A prime's groove dropped on a hunter means nothing: the sheet refuses the drop rather than accepting it silently.
groove.descriptionHint: The book's text. It is what the roll dialog and the card recall at the moment the groove can fire — including for grooves the system does not play.
groove.descriptionPlaceholder: The base rule this groove breaks, in the book's words.
groove.substitutionHint: “Always use X traits for Y or Z tests.” The traits opened are the roller's own, and never grant the genre die: it is the traits that change approach, not the test.
groove.remindersHint: What the system says without ever applying it: a groove that drives a clock or depends on a fact out of reach is recalled at the right moment, and nothing more. Fifteen grooves of the book have only that.
groove.noReminder: No reminder: everything this groove does, the system applies.
groove.reminderPlaceholder: What must be recalled at that moment, in the book's words.
groove.untilSecretHint: The activation also ends when the secret is revealed, whatever its scope. A second clock: “before the end of the mouvement OR the reveal of the secret”.
groove.replace: This character already plays {current}. Replace it with {next}?
groove.wrongAudience: {name} is a groove meant for {audience}: it cannot be placed on this sheet.
groove.correctionUnavailable: This trait correction is unavailable: the correction limit must allow it and every required trait must be woundable.

plan.title: Long Term Plan
plan.useHint: Adds this value to the Test result and removes it from the sheet when rolling.
plan.planned: Saved result added to this Test
plan.savedHint: This result may be added voluntarily to a later Test in this Session.

sessionType.name: NAME
sessionType.label: Session type
sessionType.applied: {name} is now applied to this prime.
sessionType.overwrite: Applying {name} will replace this prime's riffs, written ones included. Continue?
sessionType.dropTypeOnly: Only a Session type Item can be applied here.
sessionType.setupHint: What Big Shot has to prepare for this session type: starting rhythm, risks, cartridges. The system computes none of it — it reminds you of it when you apply the type.
sessionType.setupPlaceholder: Starting rhythm, Big Shot's risks, what changes…

roll.title: Dice pool
roll.difficultyHint: The chosen movement's threshold, hardened or softened by hand. This is what Big Shot buys with risks.
roll.diceCountHint: The dice that go out: the movement's rank, plus one per checked trait, plus the genre bonus, plus the one an advantage adds before taking it back.
roll.genreBonusHint: One extra die when the hunter's approach matches the prime's. Observed, not chosen.

actions.damageTrait: Damage this trait: it cancels one false note, and stays damaged.
actions.stakeTrait: Stake this trait: the pool is rerolled with one more die. Without both cartons, the trait is struck out until the end of the session.
actions.dented: Dented to correct a false note.
actions.broken: Struck out until the end of the session: a lost double or nothing.
actions.voidNoteHint: Remove one false note from this test, charged to nobody. Big Shot only, for when the fiction did not warrant it: it does not count against the hunter's two corrections.

roll.bonusDiceHint: Dice added by hand, for whatever the book leaves to the table: Get Involved grants two, Big Shot gives or takes at will. They belong to the pool, so a double or nothing keeps them.

dials.title: Linked dials
dials.hint: Objectives and threats accept a hunter's positive cartons or this prime's negative false notes. The GM chooses what pays.
dials.noneLinked: No dial is linked to this prime.
dials.noneVisible: No visible dial is linked to this prime.
dials.dropHint: Drag a world dial here to link it to this prime.
dials.dropDialOnly: Only a Dial Item can be linked here.
dials.dropWorldDialOnly: This dial must first be imported into the world's Items.
dials.dropLinked: {name} is now linked to this prime.
dials.noPayer: Nobody can pay for a slice on this dial.

poster.optionsHint: What this prime shows on the on-screen wanted poster while it is the one in play. Unchecking both keeps its identity secret.
poster.inactiveNote: Only shown while this prime is in play.

settings.posterPositionHint: Where the wanted poster of the prime in play hangs, for the whole table.

mono.title: MONO
mono.traitsHint: Three hexagons: the craft's name, then two free traits. They carry no genre, so they serve every roll for as long as they are not dented.
mono.none: No MONO. Drop one onto this sheet.
mono.monoFirst: The MONO's traits take the hit before the hunter's.
mono.outOfChase: Out of the chase: every MONO trait is dented.
mono.outOfChaseHint: The pilot must break off. It is the player's turn to say what happens: wreck, dead engine, ejection into the void?
mono.primeHint: This prime's ship. Purely narrative — nothing damages it — but it can be placed on a scene.

vaisseauMere.descriptorsHint: What the ship says about the campaign. No dice, no damage: two themes and a tone, as a compass.

placeholders.exterior: Painted hull, chameleon bulkheads, water tank…

activation.title: Activations
activation.hint: What this groove does, and what it takes: conditions that must all hold at once, a price chosen among the options, effects applied together, and the duration if any. All of it applies, or none.
activation.invalid: Invalid activation: it is preserved but entirely blocked

prohibitions.cartonAgainstDifficulty: spending a carton against the difficulty

activation.secretHint: Only Big Shot sees the detail of this activation; the table knows it is running, not what it does.
